name: NJ-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Chris Smith's long incumbency and name recognition
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, Smith's decades-long incumbency, and his dominant fundraising advantage over a minimally funded challenger all point to a safe Republican hold, and markets price Smith around 95%. No polls or expert ratings contradict this picture.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or an unexpected national wave could tighten the race, though Smith has survived such environments before.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving House members, seeks another term in a New Jersey district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. He has built a large financial edge, with roughly $592,000 raised and $488,000 on hand, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised only about $34,000 with minimal cash remaining. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Smith about a 95% chance of winning.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, his incumbency advantage, and the money gap all point the same direction. Smith has historically run ahead of even his district's lean, and there is no evidence of a serious challenge this cycle. The race is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
